scope: Six contact sheets (6 sampled original frames each), plus full-sized ego frames 697 and 704; not a full native-frame audit. Also inspected both full-event contact sheets (12 native frames per view) for the 14.5-second event; sampled-frame review only.

findings.finding: Compact card f0000704 says tool is on the surface and unchanged. Full-size image shows a different hand/tool position and shaft orientation compared with f0000697, including a green handle insert previously obscured. No-visible-change is unsupported; the unknown surface-separation statement also conflicts with the positive on-surface statement.
findings.scope_limit: This pair supports visible pose/orientation change; exact physical surface clearance is not quantitatively measured.

findings.finding: Verbose card uses firm grip and fully visible despite hand occlusion. Excess repeated bin/tool inventory does not establish accurate operation understanding.

Visual reference sequence: reach toward table tools; hand returns to round opening of held component; fingers positioned around rim/interior; reach toward table again. Exact tool pickup and mechanism require closer inspection; GT wrench label alone cannot resolve it.
Left hand supports metal component; right hand around mostly occluded tool/working area. Hand orientation changes. Do not infer exact fastener rotation, direction, tightness or correction.
Both hands and upright orange/red-handled tool visible at component. Supports repeated manipulation and left-hand support, with finer contact details unresolved.

Compact cards name orange pencil, motor, fan blades, rotor/stator despite insufficient fine visual evidence. The visible orange handled tool has screwdriver-like appearance; internal identity is unresolved. Also some positive contact/surface assertions conflict with unknowns. Final description and QA must not inherit these unverified fine identities.

Final QA reverses operator hand roles: the arm at image-left reaching toward tools corresponds to the operator right hand, also consistent with the bracelet in ego; component is held by operator left. The answer instead repeatedly says right holds the component, left reaches.

Final main QA claims no movement, rotation or state change and auditor marks candidate. Sampled native images show changes in right-hand/finger posture relative to the supported component; absolute no-movement statement is too strong. Actual fastener rotation/direction remains unresolved.

Dense-video repair claims the wrench is brought inside the component and removed; cited f0002910 still shows hand near tools, while f0002924/f0002932 show right fingers over the opening with wrench visible lying in background. Auditor nevertheless marks such claims supported and mismatches their frame times. These views do not justify its asserted wrench-insertion sequence. Blind two-image probe then describes hands on the component but invents a release/joining transition.
findings.scope_limit: Full-size frames inspected directly, not proof that no tool interaction occurred anywhere outside these observed instants.
